reference_items.native_verdict: Scoped to this file rather than the corpus-wide graph (out of round-1 scope). All twelve of this file's topic ids resolve and return non-empty text for the signatures driven. But game/data/dialogue/topics/50-mainline.json ALSO declares a topic record with id 'the-steward-of-the-count' (Q-MAIN-26's own entry topic) plus 'the-sill' and 'the-opening-of-the-count' -- the handover's claim 'main-quest-argument.json introduces no duplicate id' is false. converse.js buildTopicIndex() merges same-id records across files by design and scores the merged infos by specificity; the eleven-year-old third-person stub in 50-mainline.json (d:20, no race filter) outscores main-quest-argument.json's warmblood-specific first-person greeting (no d field) by 9.2 to 8.5 for any player whose race is outside {saxhleel,naga,dunmer} and whose disposition clears 20 -- reproducibly 3 of the file's own 11 documented signatures (blackrose-khajiit d36, foreign-born-nord d30, foreign-born-imperial d24), 2 of which are in the piece's own shipped act5-argument-probe.mjs test set, which reported ok:true regardless because its checks only ask whether SOME text returns, never whether the returned text is this file's own. build-graph.mjs's unreachable-INFO lint (step 4) also misses it because it only flags a strict filter superset, not a cross-file id collision plus specificity-score win. Per this item's own scoring rule ('Any orphan, or any unreachable INFO -> FAIL, automatic, no score'), this is exactly that class of defect on this file's own entry line.

biggest_gap.what: game/data/dialogue/topics/50-mainline.json and game/data/dialogue/topics/main-quest-argument.json both declare a topic record with id 'the-steward-of-the-count' -- Q-MAIN-26's own opens_by.topic and the entry line of the whole Act V climax. converse.js buildTopicIndex() merges same-id records across files by design; infoFor()'s specificity score (matchesActor 8 + requires 4 + dScore + forbids 0.5) lets the older file's ungated-race, d:20 third-person stub ('Ixtu-Meer. He has kept the Count...', score 9.2) outscore the newer file's race-specific, undated warmblood greeting (score 8.5) for any player whose race is outside {saxhleel,naga,dunmer} and whose disposition clears 20.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: This is the very first line Ixtu-Meer speaks in the scene the whole main quest builds to, and for a majority of the playable race roster (7 of 10 races are outside the exempt set, and most upbringings clear disposition 20) it is not what the file's author wrote -- it is a flat, third-person stub referring to the speaker by name as if reporting on him to somebody else. It is invisible to check-quests.mjs, check-content.mjs, and build-graph.mjs's unreachable-INFO lint (all three passed clean), and it was invisible to the piece's own shipped probe, which tested 2 of the 3 affected signatures and still reported ok:true, because none of these instruments ever compares the returned text against the text the file that owns the topic actually authored.

remedy.action: Resolve the 3-way id collision between main-quest-argument.json and 50-mainline.json (delete 50-mainline.json's now-superseded the-steward-of-the-count/the-sill/the-opening-of-the-count stubs, or rename this file's three quest-entry ids so no other file shares them and update hooks.json/NPC topics[] to match); give the entry info a d value at or above the stub's, or add a tie-break in converse.js infoFor() so an actor-matched race-gated info always outranks an actor-matched race-blind one regardless of d; add a check alongside build-graph.mjs's unreachable-INFO lint that, for a named hand-authored file, asserts the info actually delivered to every documented signature is one of that file's own infos rather than a merged stranger's; and either give keeper-ei-vashan and gallery-intake-keepers a post.site that is not stone-wastes-count, or move their two overlapping topic ids off this file's twelve.
remedy.acceptance: gen-converse-node-repro.mjs Part A shows 0 of 11 documented signatures receiving the 50-mainline.json stub on the-steward-of-the-count (currently 3 of 11), and Part B shows 0 of 2 sibling rootkeeper records able to deliver any of the twelve Act-V topic ids once each is given a spawn point (currently 2 of 2 can).

secondary_observations.what: check-prose.mjs --file: sting 0.00/10k and fragopen 0.00/10k, both below the corpus reference and both explicitly non-waivable per the file's own prose_register_exemption_note -- the corpus-wide 'every line lands a punchline' defect does not appear in this file. The single question mark in 3,635 words is Ixtu-Meer posing his own rhetorical question and answering it, demonstrating the voice_note's claim rather than merely declaring it.

The antagonist's strongest case (closing the sill-gate kills the wells within a season; opening it fully gives the wells everything once and then nothing ever) is backed by a genuine cost on the 'good' ending: res_open_the_count's own outcome text and world_flags (wells_reissue_degraded_province_wide, tithe_gourd_charges_reduced) show the province worse off in a measurable way even in the ending that vindicates the Court. A reasonable player has textual grounds to prefer res_take_his_place or res_walk_out.

The-ninth-clause-of-the-drowned-tally's d20 reveal ('I have never written in the Recension... it serves either argument exactly as well as the other') was checked against mainline.json's own adjudication_audit, independently, and the claim of neutrality holds: no quest, book, NPC line or ending in the tree adjudicates the ninth clause.

path_to_ten: (a) Resolve the id collision with 50-mainline.json (delete its now-superseded stubs for the-steward-of-the-count/the-sill/the-opening-of-the-count, or rename this file's three quest-entry ids and repoint hooks.json/NPC topics[]). (b) Give the entry info a d value competitive with the stub, or fix converse.js infoFor()'s specificity score so a race-gated actor line cannot lose to a race-blind one purely on an unrelated disposition floor. (c) Add a lint alongside build-graph.mjs's unreachable-INFO check that verifies, for each hand-authored file, that the text delivered to its own documented signatures is its own text -- the failure shape here (cross-file id merge + specificity-score win) is invisible to the existing strict-superset lint. (d) Give keeper-ei-vashan and gallery-intake-keepers a post.site outside stone-wastes-count, or move their overlapping topic ids off this file's twelve, so a future W1-GIVER-PRESENCE placement pass cannot hand Ixtu-Meer's personal confession to a background NPC. (e) Once W1-19/W1-VIABILITY-SPLIT's Q-MAIN-06 reveal-writer gap is fixed and a walked character can actually reach Act V, re-run RI-EXP05 Steps 1-9 in full including the Step 6 blind pair -- this piece's content is ready for that measurement; the game currently is not.

notes: The writing is the strongest thing this piece produced: the antagonist has a real case (the allowance argument survives contact with the game's own cost accounting on the 'good' ending), the game genuinely does not refute him, the prose-tic bars that are never waivable (sting, fragopen) are clean rather than merely declared clean, and the single question mark in 3,635 words is doing characterisation rather than dodging a metric. What undercuts it is structural rather than literary: the file was authored against an id namespace it does not fully control, and the merge-by-design behaviour of converse.js's topic index lets an old stub outscore and replace the very first line of the scene for most of the playable cast, invisibly, past every existing check including the piece's own shipped probe. That is the kind of gap this project's RULES.md exists to catch -- a probe that seeds or checks only what it already expects to find.
